display.title: Episode 310: Why We Shake During Prayer
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi launches a tzedakah drawing contest, welcomes a Shema guest from Sydney, Australia, and tells how the young Frierdiker Rebbe tested his father, the Rebbe Rashab.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by announcing a new drawing contest: draw a picture about the mitzvah of tzedakah, such as giving to a poor person, inviting a guest to a meal or a decorated pushka, and win a Moshiach Times magazine and a new tzedakah box for your Tzivos Hashem room. After the Hakochainik march, a girl visiting all the way from Sydney, Australia recites the Shema. Uncle Yossi then asks why we shake the lulav and why Jews sway when they daven. The story: the young Yosef Yitzchak, later the Frierdiker Rebbe, hears his father, the Rebbe Rashab, say at a farbrengen that he can tell a Jew just by looking. He trains a Jewish friend and a well-mannered non-Jewish boy to read Ashrei identically and dresses them alike, yet his father picks out the Jewish boy at once. The answer: at Mattan Torah the people trembled, and that sway before Hashem has passed down to every Jew. The show closes with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: Swaying in prayer is part of every Jew's identity from Har Sinai; when we 'shake' with more Torah and good deeds, Hashem will shake Moshiach into coming.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: Shabbos candles on Friday, January 15; 'in the spirit of Hakhel'.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full, with her parents and city.

sources_cited.note: Quoted by the Rebbe Rashab: both the soul and the body of a Jew are holy.
At Mattan Torah the people saw and trembled; the source of swaying in prayer.

segments.title: Uncle Yossi's Mitzvah Contest: draw a tzedakah picture
segments.summary: Children are invited to draw a picture about tzedakah and mail it in to win a magazine and a tzedakah box.

segments.title: Shema with a guest from Sydney, Australia
Why We Shake the Lulav, and Why We Shuckle
segments.summary: Shaking the lulav in six directions shows trust in Hashem; swaying is a sign of life and of being a Yid.

segments.title: The Rebbe Rashab and the Two Boys
segments.summary: The young Yosef Yitzchak trains two boys to read Ashrei identically, but his father tells the Jewish boy by the way he sways.

segments.title: A Good Shake for Moshiach
segments.summary: When we shake ourselves into more Torah and mitzvos, Hashem will bring the Geulah.
